# The critical logarithmic-derivative kernel is a complete two-channel Weil resolvent family

- **ID:** `critical-logderivative-two-channel-weil-resolvent-law`
- **Stage:** 3-formalized
- **Type:** THEOREM (Lean), `[BRIDGE]`

  two-channel family is complete for RH: its positivity is equivalent to the full Weil criterion.

## Centered divisor and Weil polarization

Put

```text
X(w)=xi(1/2+w),
L(w)=X'(w)/X(w).                                           (1)
```

For every nontrivial zero `rho`, write

```text
alpha_rho=(rho-1/2)/i,                                    (2)
```

so that `X(i alpha_rho)=0`. The centered divisor is invariant under

```text
alpha -> -alpha,
alpha -> conjugate(alpha).                                (3)
```

For Weil-admissible functions `F,G`, use the polarized form

```text
q_W(F,G)
 =sum_rho m_rho F(alpha_rho)G#(alpha_rho),

G#(z)=conjugate(G(conjugate(z))).                          (4)
```

By the completed explicit formula, `(4)` is also defined from the full von Mangoldt tail plus the
Gamma, pole, and normalization terms.

## Canonical resolvent channels

For `Re w>1/2`, define

```text
A_w(z)=w/(w^2+z^2),
B_w(z)=z/(w^2+z^2).                                       (5)
```

Every nontrivial centered zero satisfies `|Im alpha_rho|<1/2`. The poles `z=+-iw` of `(5)` are
therefore outside the closed zero strip. Products of two channels have quadratic decay on
horizontal strips, so they belong to the standard completed Weil class. In particular, all
pairings below are source-defined by the explicit formula.

Equivalently, put

```text
R_w^+(z)=1/(w-iz),
R_w^-(z)=1/(w+iz).                                        (6)
```

Then

```text
A_w=(R_w^++R_w^-)/2,
B_w=(R_w^+-R_w^-)/(2i).                                   (7)
```

These are the two Hardy resolvent orientations forced by functional-equation parity.

## Exact resolvent--Weil identity

`[PROVED]` For `Re w,Re v>1/2`,

```text
(L(w)+conjugate(L(v)))/(w+conjugate(v))
 =q_W(A_w,A_v)+q_W(B_w,B_v)                               (8)

 =1/2*(q_W(R_w^+,R_v^+)+q_W(R_w^-,R_v^-)).                (9)
```

### Proof

The even entire function `X` has the paired Hadamard product

```text
X(w)/X(0)
 =product_(alpha mod +-)(1+w^2/alpha^2)^(m_alpha),         (10)
```

with locally uniform convergence after the standard symmetric ordering; convergence follows from
the exponent-two summability of the centered divisor. Logarithmic differentiation gives

```text
L(w)
 =sum_(alpha mod +-)
    2m_alpha w/(w^2+alpha^2).                              (11)
```

Reality of `X` gives `conjugate(L(v))=L(conjugate(v))`. For each `+-` orbit, elementary algebra
gives

```text
1/(w+conjugate(v))
 *(2w/(w^2+alpha^2)
   +2conjugate(v)/(conjugate(v)^2+alpha^2))

 =2(w conjugate(v)+alpha^2)
   /((w^2+alpha^2)(conjugate(v)^2+alpha^2)).               (12)
```

On the other hand,

```text
A_v#(alpha)=conjugate(v)/(conjugate(v)^2+alpha^2),
B_v#(alpha)=alpha/(conjugate(v)^2+alpha^2).                (13)
```

Hence the contribution of `alpha` to the right side of `(8)` is

```text
(w conjugate(v)+alpha^2)
 /((w^2+alpha^2)(conjugate(v)^2+alpha^2)).                 (14)
```

The same value occurs at `-alpha`. Summing the two points in every orbit turns `(14)` into `(12)`,
including multiplicity. Summing all orbits proves `(8)`. Equation `(9)` follows from `(7)` by
polarization; the cross terms cancel.

For nodes `w_1,...,w_N` in `Re w>1/2` and coefficients `c_1,...,c_N`, put

```text
A_c=sum_j c_j A_(w_j),
B_c=sum_j c_j B_(w_j).                                    (15)
```

Then the following are equivalent:

```text
(i)  RH;

(ii) q_W(A_c,A_c)+q_W(B_c,B_c)>=0

(iii) the kernel
      K_L(w,v)=(L(w)+conjugate(L(v)))/(w+conjugate(v))
```

/-!
# Rank-one detection of an off-critical zero by the Weil form

An off-critical zero makes the Weil form on the resolvent test algebra indefinite,
and a single base point already witnesses it.

Writing `A z = conj z / (z (z − conj z))`, Schwarz reality of the centered completed
zeta turns the diagonal Weil value into the real expression

`Q z = M₁ − 2 Re (A z · logDeriv XiC z)`,

with `M₁` the second inverse moment of the divisor.  Near a zero `pt₀` off the real
axis the logarithmic derivative has a simple pole of positive integer residue while
`A` stays finite and nonzero — the two poles of the conjugate pair are at distinct
points precisely because the zero is off the line.  Approaching `pt₀` along the ray
`pt₀ + t·A pt₀·m` therefore drives `Q` to `−∞`.
-/

open Complex Filter Topology Metric

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

/-! ## §1 Local pole structure of `logDeriv XiC` -/

/-- Around any point the centered completed zeta peels on a small ball with a
nonvanishing analytic cofactor. -/
theorem XiC_peel_ball (pt₀ : ℂ) :
    ∃ R > 0, ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (ball pt₀ R) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ ball pt₀ R, g z ≠ 0) ∧
      ∀ z ∈ ball pt₀ R,
        XiC z = (z - pt₀) ^ (analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat * g z := by
  have hm : analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀ =
      ((analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat : ℕ∞) :=
    (ENat.coe_toNat (XiC_order_ne_top pt₀)).symm
  obtain ⟨g, hgan, hg0, hfact, -⟩ :=
    exists_peel isOpen_univ XiC_analytic (Set.mem_univ pt₀) hm
  have hcont : ContinuousAt g pt₀ := (hgan pt₀ (Set.mem_univ pt₀)).continuousAt
  have hev : ∀ᶠ z in nhds pt₀, g z ≠ 0 := hcont.eventually_ne hg0
  obtain ⟨R, hR, hball⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.mp hev
  refine ⟨R, hR, g, fun z _ => hgan z (Set.mem_univ z), ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro z hz
    exact hball (by rwa [mem_ball] at hz)
  · intro z _
    exact hfact z (Set.mem_univ z)

/-- The vanishing order at a zero is positive. -/
theorem XiC_order_toNat_pos {pt₀ : ℂ} (h0 : XiC pt₀ = 0) :
    0 < (analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat := by
  obtain ⟨R, hR, g, hgan, hg0, hfact⟩ := XiC_peel_ball pt₀
  by_contra hcon
  push Not at hcon
  have hzero : (analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat = 0 := by omega
  have hval := hfact pt₀ (mem_ball_self hR)
  rw [hzero, pow_zero, one_mul] at hval
  exact hg0 pt₀ (mem_ball_self hR) (by rw [← hval, h0])

/-- **Pole splitting.**  On a punctured ball around a zero the logarithmic
derivative is the simple pole of residue the vanishing order plus an analytic
remainder. -/
theorem logDeriv_XiC_eq_pole_add {pt₀ : ℂ} {R : ℝ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hgan : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ g (ball pt₀ R))
    (hg0 : ∀ z ∈ ball pt₀ R, g z ≠ 0)
    (hfact : ∀ z ∈ ball pt₀ R,
      XiC z = (z - pt₀) ^ (analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat * g z)
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball pt₀ R) (hzne : z ≠ pt₀) :
    logDeriv XiC z =
      ((analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat : ℂ) / (z - pt₀) + logDeriv g z := by
  set m := (analyticOrderAt XiC pt₀).toNat with hm
  have hsub : z - pt₀ ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hzne
  have hpow : (z - pt₀) ^ m ≠ 0 := pow_ne_zero _ hsub
  have hgz : g z ≠ 0 := hg0 z hz
  have hopen : IsOpen (ball pt₀ R) := isOpen_ball
  have hev : XiC =ᶠ[nhds z]
      fun w : ℂ => (w - pt₀) ^ m * g w :=
    Filter.eventually_of_mem (hopen.mem_nhds hz) fun w hw => hfact w hw
  have hdpow : DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w : ℂ => (w - pt₀) ^ m) z := by
    fun_prop
  have hdg : DifferentiableAt ℂ g z :=
    (hgan z hz).differentiableAt
  have hlog : logDeriv XiC z =
      logDeriv (fun w : ℂ => (w - pt₀) ^ m * g w) z := by
    rw [logDeriv, logDeriv, Pi.div_apply, Pi.div_apply, hev.deriv_eq,
      hfact z hz]
  rw [hlog, logDeriv_mul z hpow hgz hdpow hdg]
  congr 1
  have hderiv : HasDerivAt (fun w : ℂ => (w - pt₀) ^ m)
      ((m : ℂ) * (z - pt₀) ^ (m - 1)) z := by
    have h := ((hasDerivAt_id z).sub_const pt₀).pow m
    simpa using! h
  rw [logDeriv, Pi.div_apply, hderiv.deriv]
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos m with hm0 | hmpos
  · simp [hm0]
  · rw [div_eq_div_iff hpow hsub]
    have hsplit : (z - pt₀) ^ m = (z - pt₀) ^ (m - 1) * (z - pt₀) := by
      rw [← pow_succ]
      congr 1
      omega
    rw [hsplit]
    ring

/-! ## §2 The diagonal Weil value as a real expression -/

/-- Schwarz reality of the logarithmic derivative in the centered coordinate.
The divisor is invariant under conjugation of the centered coordinate, so
reindexing the relative resolvent trace along that involution conjugates it. -/
theorem logDeriv_XiC_conj {z : ℂ} (hz : XiC z ≠ 0) :
    logDeriv XiC ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) = (starRingEnd ℂ) (logDeriv XiC z) := by
  have hzc : XiC ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) ≠ 0 := XiC_ne_zero_conj hz
  rw [logDeriv_XiC_eq_relativeResolventTrace hz,
    logDeriv_XiC_eq_relativeResolventTrace hzc, xiRelativeResolventTrace,
    xiRelativeResolventTrace, Complex.conj_tsum]
  rw [← (xiZeroCopyLineConjEquiv).tsum_eq
    (fun q => xiRelativeResolventTerm ((starRingEnd ℂ) z) q)]
  refine tsum_congr fun q => ?_

# Cofinal admissible rectangles for the centered Xi divisor

Every centered Xi spectral point has imaginary coordinate strictly between `-1/2` and `1/2`.
Given any finite packet of multiplicity copies, this module constructs a rectangle containing the
packet strictly in its interior whose whole boundary is admissible for the continued
prime--archimedean explicit formula.

The construction uses only finite avoidance.  A raw compact rectangle contains finitely many Xi
zeros; the final left, right, and top coordinates are selected from open intervals while avoiding
the finite sets of their real and imaginary coordinates.  The bottom edge is fixed below the Xi
strip.  Thus the admissible rectangles are cofinal among finite divisor packets.

# Pole centering preserves the actual phase defect

Zeta has exact critical reflection and the literal pole residue is real.
Subtracting their product leaves the reflection defect unchanged, including
at source zeros. The signed centered square therefore measures the gap
between twice the centered physical energy and the actual canonical phase cost.

private theorem centered_unitary_square {u z : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) :
    ‖u * z - conj z‖ ^ 2 = 2 * ‖z‖ ^ 2 - 2 * (u * z ^ 2).re := by
  have hh := Complex.normSq_sub (u * z) (conj z)
  simp only [Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq, norm_mul, hu, one_mul,
    Complex.norm_conj, starRingEnd_self_apply] at hh

private theorem critical_zeta_reflection (t : ℝ) :
    zetaChi (1 - tracePoint 0 t) * riemannZeta (tracePoint 0 t) =
      conj (riemannZeta (tracePoint 0 t)) := by
  have hs : 1 - tracePoint 0 t = conj (tracePoint 0 t) := by
    apply Complex.ext <;> norm_num [tracePoint]
